answer: On frost nights the watchmen light the braziers between the rows, and each man logs the hours he kept his fire burning. A prism night claimed as watched fails the log: the brazier must have burned at the harbor of the row, and a cold brazier tells the story at dawn. Faking a winter of frost watch means hiring watchmen, burning three tons of wood and paying 10,300, while the basalt book in the watch hut is read at every bud-break, so a row whose fire was never lit is left to the frost.
